title: A proof run passed only when it is verified and every automated test record passed
when: With a spec of four automated test records and one that is not: proofRunPassed reads a verified proof run in which every automated test record passed and the other failed; one in which a test failed, one did not run, one was skipped and one has no outcome; and no verified proof run, with and without automated test records.
then: The first passed with no reason. The second gives one reason for each automated test record that did not pass, in ID order, and none for the record that is not automated. With no verified proof run, the one reason says so, also when the spec has no automated test record.

title: An attestation is verified only for the commit, the proof run type and the trusted signer at a grade the change allows
when: attestationVerified checks a proof run statement signed by proof-run.yml at main, with the workflows folder as the base's and changed; signed at the change's own reference, with the folder as the base's and changed; and statements with a subject digest or name of another commit, two subjects, no subject, another predicate type, a proof run about another commit, a predicate that is not JSON, another workflow, another repository, another issuer, another pull request's reference, a branch that is not main, a tag, no reference, a certificate of another source repository, a source ref that is not the signer's, and a statement signed at main by a run at another commit or at no commit. Then a statement signed at the change's own reference by a run at another commit. Then a pull request's statement with no change reference to gate, and main as the change's reference.
then: The statement signed at main is release grade with either folder. The one at the change's own reference is change grade with the base's folder, and is refused with change grade, naming each changed file, with a changed folder. Each other statement is refused with no grade, and so is the pull request's with no change reference. A statement signed at main by a run at another commit than its subject is refused; a change-grade one by a run at another commit keeps change grade.

title: A change holds the ratchet unless an obligation present at the base lost a share, new obligations may arrive with none, and a retirement carries a removed obligation's standing to its successor
when: holdsRatchet compares a base with obligations of each standing to a change that keeps or gains every share and adds an obligation with no share and one only designed; then to a change under which obligations fall from one or two shares, one with every share is absent, one with no share is absent, and one with no share stays with none; then to a change with retirements: one moves an obligation to a successor with each of its shares, one moves an obligation to two successors of which one is not built, one names no successor, and one names an obligation the base does not have, while one more obligation is absent with no retirement; then to changes that rename a pattern rule that two domains follow under a retirement, first with its successor proved in each domain where the rule was, then with the successor not proved in one of them.
then: The first change holds the ratchet. The second gives one reason per share fallen, by obligation ID and then designed, built, proved. The absent obligation with shares gives one reason that it is absent at the change, with the shares it had at the base; the obligations with no share give none. The third gives one reason that names the retirement, the successor and the share it does not have, and the reason that the obligation with no retirement is absent; it follows the retirement to the successor with each share and the retirement with no successor, and gives them by the retired obligation's ID; it does not follow the retirement of an obligation the base does not have. A retirement's reason takes its place among the obligations' reasons in the fixed order. A retirement of a pattern rule names the rule in each domain and compares the successor in the same domain: the first rename holds the ratchet, the second gives one reason that names the rule and its successor with that domain, and the retirement is reported once.

title: A commit is fully proved only when it has an obligation, every share is 100% and a proof run at it passed
when: fullyProved reads a measurement in which every obligation has every share with a passed proof run; then obligations that lack one, two or all shares with a proof run in which a test failed and one has no outcome; then no verified proof run; then a commit with no obligation, with a passed proof run and with none.
then: The first is fully proved with no reason. The second gives one reason per share each obligation lacks, by obligation ID and then designed, built, proved, then the test records that did not pass, in the fixed order. With no verified proof run, the one reason says why. The commit with no obligation is not fully proved: its first reason says that a release needs at least one obligation, and with no proof run the reason for that follows. A proof run signed at a ref other than main never reaches fullyProved: VerifyAttestation refuses it for the release gate, by its ref (ST-ASR-UC03-R05-T01).

title: Package of two domains is found in a tree built for it, and not in one that follows the rule
when: Lists each package and the domains whose records name its files.
then: Expects the package that two domains name to be found with both domains, and a package one domain and a shared value type name not to be.

title: Identifier missing from its file is found in a tree built for it, and not in one that follows the rule
when: Parses the files named by predicate, handler, service, value type, data model, event type, projection, repository, table and CLI handler records, and passes over a CLI command, which is not of the technical stage.
then: Expects a record whose identifier the file declares to pass, and one whose identifier is absent, or declared in another file, to be found.

title: Import against the order is found in a tree built for it, and not in one that follows the rule
when: Reads the import graph of every package under internal and cmd and the domain each package belongs to, from the records that name its files.
then: Expects an import along the order to pass, a reverse import to be found with both packages and domains, and a cmd package's imports to pass.

title: Test without its ID is found in a tree built for it, and not in one that follows the rule
when: Parses every test file under the product root for test and subtest names, and reads every automated test record.
then: Expects a test file whose subtests carry IDs to pass, a test file with none to be found, and a test record whose file lacks its ID to be found.

title: Source file without a record is found in a tree built for it, and not in one that follows the rule
when: Lists the source files of a tree and the files and folders every technical record names. Then it lists, from the real Lathe's meta model, each kind of Lathe's own technical stage that has a file column.
then: Expects a file a record names to pass, a file under a folder a record names to pass, and a file no record reaches to be found. Expects the kinds whose records the rule reads to be exactly Lathe's own technical kinds with a file column, so no technical record is missed.

title: Stub counted as built is found in a tree built for it, and not in one that follows the rule
when: Parses the function each predicate, handler and service record names.
then: Expects a function that reads a parameter to pass, and one whose body is only a constant return, or only a panic, to be found.

title: A record whose canonical bytes do not hash to the trusted digest is refused
when: With a build record on disk, and a trusted digest: Verify runs with a digest that is not the record's; then with a record that carries a duplicate field whose bytes hash to the digest given.
then: The first is refused naming the digest; the second is refused as not canonical.

title: An image signature is acceptable only in the log or by a trusted key, and by the trusted signer
when: With a verified attestation about one image digest, by the trusted keyless signer and in the transparency log: AcceptableSignature runs on it, on one by the trusted key with no log entry, and on each of these changes: no log entry, another image, two subjects, another workflow, another reference, another issuer, another key, no signing time, no trusted signer; and on the result that gh attestation verify prints.
then: The keyless signature in the log and the signature by the trusted key are accepted; each change is refused; the printed result gives the subject, the signer, the log index and the time, and an empty, double, non in-toto or negative-index result is refused.

title: A declaration that leaves a default with no reason satisfies it, and one that gives a reason does not
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD02 with tenancy kind single and no reason; with audit off and no reason; with each of these and a reason; with tenancy pooled and audit on and no reason; and TD02 unchanged.
then: Expects the first two to satisfy it, and the others not to satisfy it.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name.

title: A tenancy claim whose first name is a request part satisfies it, and a token claim path does not
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD02 with each of these tenancy claims: header.X-Tenant-ID; BODY.org_id; request.body.org_id; org.id; and headerx.org.
then: Expects the first three to satisfy it, and org.id and headerx.org not to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name. Decision on review item 8 of the Declaring test plan: a tenancy claim has a token claim path grammar, and checking refuses the forms that name a request part (ST-DECL-EN09). headerx.org catches a check by a string prefix.

title: Tenants none, a collection over a system entity and a tenant binding that writes a shared entity each satisfy it
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD02 with a controller with tenants none; a collection over an entity with tenant system; a binding that runs as tenant on a collection with create over an entity with tenant shared; and then with tenants each, a collection over an owned entity, and the binding run as system.
then: Expects each of the first three to satisfy it, and the last three not to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name.

title: An unknown audit level, an audit sink that is no port binding and an unknown sensitivity each satisfy it
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD02 with audit level verbose; with an audit sink that is no port binding; with the sensitivity confidential; and then with level metadata, level change, a bound sink, and each of public, pii and secret.
then: Expects each of the first three to satisfy it, and none of the others to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name.

title: A resource type, permission, relation or caveat parameter the compiled schema lacks each satisfy it
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD03 and its compiled schema with one change each: an entity with the resource type archive; a collection operation with the permission destroy; a binding that names the relation approver; and an entity with the context field request.region. Then it reads TD03 unchanged.
then: Expects each of the four changes to satisfy it, and TD03 unchanged not to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name.

title: A written relation the schema lacks, or of a type no entity declares, satisfies it
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD03 with a binding whose Relationships written is document#approver; then folder#viewer; then document#viewer.
then: Expects the first two to satisfy it, and document#viewer not to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name.

title: A value for a setting or a slot input that the component's schema marks as a bypass satisfies it, and a value for an unmarked one does not
when: With a copy of the registry of ST-DECL-TD01 in which, written into its files and not through stego registry add, the config schema of the authorization component declares two settings, skip_authz marked as a bypass and cache_ttl not marked, and the slot before_create of rest-api declares two inputs, skip_check marked as a bypass and note not marked: the predicate reads ST-DECL-TD03 with skip_authz: true in the settings of the authorization component; with skip_check: true on a binding at before_create; with cache_ttl: 30s; with note: hello on a binding; and TD03 unchanged.
then: Expects the first two to satisfy it, and the last three not to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name. Decision of the Product owner on review item 7 of the Declaring test plan: a bypass flag is a value for a setting or slot input that the component's schema marks as a bypass; the registry refuses to publish such a component (ST-SUP-UC01-R07), so the fixture writes the registry files directly. The unmarked setting and input catch a check by a list of names; a fault of the undeclared rules (ST-DECL-INV02, ST-DECL-INV12) cannot occur, because each name is declared.

title: Required on with read, list, update or delete satisfies it, and create or patch does not
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD02 with idempotency required on create and read; create and list; create and update; create and delete; create; and create and patch.
then: Expects the first four to satisfy it, and the last two not to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Update is served by PUT (decision on ST-DECL-Q01).

title: A money field typed as a float or a decimal satisfies it, and integer minor units with a currency do not
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD04 with a money field price typed as a float; as a decimal; and as integer minor units in EUR.
then: Expects the float and the decimal to satisfy it, and the integer minor units not to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name.

title: A ledger with no currency, a non-ISO currency or a minimum balance in another currency satisfies it
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD04 with no currency; with the currency EURO; with the minimum balance of customer_wallet in USD; and TD04 unchanged.
then: Expects the first three to satisfy it, and TD04 unchanged not to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name.

title: A ledger collection with update or delete satisfies it, and one with only the six ledger operations does not
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD04 with update added to the transfers collection; with delete added; and TD04 unchanged, whose collection allows create, post, void, reverse, read and list.
then: Expects the first two to satisfy it, and TD04 unchanged not to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name.

title: A mode other than api, worker or controller satisfies it
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD02 with the modes api and batch; with api, worker and controller; with worker only; and with no modes.
then: Expects the first to satisfy it, and the other three not to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name.

title: kafka-events without durable-events satisfies it
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD02 with the mixin kafka-events alone; with kafka-events and durable-events; with durable-events alone; and with no mixin.
then: Expects the first to satisfy it, and the other three not to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name.

title: A declared invariant of another kind, or without the fields its kind needs, satisfies it
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD02 with a declared invariant of the kind exclusive; unique with no by; no_overlap with no range; sum_limit with no parent; and then unique with on and by, no_overlap with on, range and by, and sum_limit with on and parent.
then: Expects each of the first four to satisfy it, and none of the last three to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name.

title: A controller with no lease TTL, a source other than scan or watch, or tenants other than each satisfies it
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD02 with a controller with no lease TTL; with the source poll; with tenants none; and with sources scan and watch, a lease TTL and tenants each.
then: Expects each of the first three to satisfy it, and the last not to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name.

title: With authorization bound, an entity with no resource type or an operation with no permission satisfies it
when: The predicate reads ST-DECL-TD03 with Todo given no resource type; with no permission for list; with list public and no reason; with list public and a reason; TD03 unchanged; and TD02, which binds no authorization and gives Todo no resource type.
then: Expects the first three to satisfy it, and the last three not to.
notes: Not automated yet: the predicate is not built. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name.

title: A digest is superseded only when its lifecycle holds a supersession
when: Reads the lifecycles of a digest with a supersession whose fail date is ahead, with a supersession whose fail date is past, with a withdrawal only, and with no record.
then: Expects the first two to be superseded, and the last two not.

title: A digest is past its fail date only after the date of its supersession or withdrawal
when: Reads, on the day 2026-06-01, the lifecycles of a digest with a supersession that fails after 2026-05-31, after 2026-06-01 and after 2026-06-02; with a withdrawal that fails after 2026-05-31 and after 2026-06-02; and with no record.
then: Expects the supersession and the withdrawal that fail after 2026-05-31 to be past their fail date. Expects the others not to be: a digest is not past its date on the date itself.
notes: The day is given to the predicate, so the test needs no clock.

title: A digest is withdrawn when its lifecycle holds a withdrawal, whatever its date
when: Reads the lifecycles of a digest with a withdrawal whose fail date is ahead, with one whose fail date is past, with a supersession only, and with no record.
then: Expects the first two to be withdrawn, and the last two not.

title: A requirement is met only when the environment file supplies its name, its kind and every part of its shape
when: With the requirement secret orders-database with the keys url and password, and the requirement egress payments with a port: the predicate runs on environment entries that (a) supply the secret with both keys, (b) supply the secret with the key url only, (c) supply both keys under the name orders-db, (d) supply a configuration value named orders-database, (e) supply the egress payments with an address and a port, and (f) supply the egress payments with an address and no port.
then: Expects that (a) and (e) are met, and that (b), (c), (d) and (f) are not met, each with the part that is missing: the key password, the name orders-database, the kind secret, and the port.

title: A pipeline reference is pinned only by a full commit hash or a sha256 digest
when: The predicate runs on references whose pins are a 40-character hexadecimal commit, sha256: with 64 hexadecimal characters, the tag v1.2.0, the branch main, the short hash 0123456, a 39-character hash, sha256: with 63 characters, and a sha512: digest.
then: Expects that only the 40-character commit and the 64-character sha256 digest are pinned, and that each other reference is not pinned.

title: A fill is qualified only when its evidence names both current digests and a listed key signed that evidence
when: With a fill whose evidence names its current fill digest and contract digest, and whose sign-off listed-ssh made over that evidence: ask fill.IsQualified of it and of six copies, each with one thing changed. The evidence names an earlier fill digest. The evidence names an earlier contract digest. The fill has no evidence. The fill has evidence and no sign-off. unlisted-ssh made the sign-off. The sign-off signs the digest of other evidence.
then: Expects true for the first fill, and false for each of the six copies.
notes: Not automated yet: fill.IsQualified is not written. Give the predicate real signatures by the keys of ST-EXT-TD02, so that a predicate that does not verify the signature fails the last two cases.

title: A fill fits a binding only when it implements the bound slot and serves the bound collection
when: With a binding of rest-api.before_create for org-users, and a test registry with a second component, other-api, that also declares a slot before_create: ask fill.FitsBinding of four fills. One implements rest-api.before_create for org-users. One implements rest-api.before_delete for org-users. One implements rest-api.before_create for org-groups. One implements other-api.before_create for org-users.
then: Expects true for the first fill and false for each of the other three.
notes: Not automated yet: fill.FitsBinding is not written. The fourth case catches a check that compares the slot name alone.

title: A hand-edited generated file is named as modified
when: With a project with applied output: One generated file is edited by hand and drift detection runs.
then: Exactly that file is listed as modified.

title: Every archetype and mixin of the shipped registry includes only ga components
when: Loads every archetype and mixin from the registry folder and evaluates the specification for each component they include. Then evaluates it for a fixture archetype that includes a beta component.
then: Expects every shipped component to satisfy it, so the count of experiments on golden paths is 0, and expects the fixture archetype refused with the component and its stage named.
notes: Measures ST-BO06 on every registry release: the count it keeps at 0 is the first part of the measure. The fixture archetype is refused when the registry loads.

title: A port has one provider only when exactly one component of the active component set provides it
when: Evaluates the specification for store-port over three active component sets: one in which no component provides it, one in which store-a alone provides it, and one in which store-a and store-b both provide it. Then evaluates it for every port over the set with store-a alone, where auth-port is provided by auth-a.
then: Expects it to hold only for the set with store-a alone. Expects the set with no provider to be reported with store-port and no provider, and the set with two to be reported with store-port, store-a and store-b. Expects every port of the last set to hold.
notes: The specification is over the active component set of one service (ST-SUP-TM08), not the whole registry, so a port that only the registry holds is not in the set.

title: A set answers its ports only when every port that a component of it requires has a provider in it
when: Evaluates the specification over three sets: api-a with store-a and auth-a; api-a with store-a and no provider of auth-port; and api-a alone, with no provider of store-port or auth-port.
then: Expects it to hold for the first set only. Expects the second set to be reported with auth-port, and the third with both store-port and auth-port.
notes: The third set has two unanswered ports, so an evaluation that stops at the first fails the test.

title: A component is past its sunset only when it is alpha or beta and its sunset date is earlier than today
when: With today fixed at 2026-11-04, evaluates the specification for: a beta component with the sunset 2026-11-03; a beta component with the sunset 2026-11-04; an alpha component with the sunset 2026-11-05; an alpha component with the sunset 2026-10-01; and a ga component that holds the sunset 2026-10-01.
then: Expects it to hold for the beta component of 2026-11-03 and the alpha component of 2026-10-01 only. The sunset of today is not past, and a ga component is never past its sunset.
notes: The test gives the date of today to the predicate; it does not read the clock.

title: A component states its place only with one layer, its part in a request flow and a side for every port
when: Evaluates the specification for api-a, which requires store-port and auth-port: with its full role; with two layers; with no part in a request flow; with a side for store-port and none for auth-port; and with no role at all. Then evaluates it for store-a, which provides store-port: with its full role, and with no side for store-port.
then: Expects it to hold for the full role of api-a and of store-a only, and each other case to be reported with the part that is missing or extra.
notes: api-a has two required ports, so a check that reads only the first port fails the test; store-a has a provided port, so a check that reads only the required ports fails the test.

title: An emitted file is static only when two contrasting renders give the same bytes after the module path and the package name are normalised
when: Evaluates the specification for four pairs of renders of one file from the two declarations of ST-SUP-TD04: the same bytes; bytes that differ only in the module path and the package name; bytes that differ in a line that a setting gives; and bytes that differ only in a last newline.
then: Expects it to hold for the first two pairs only.
notes: Normalising replaces only the module path and the package name, so a normalising that removes white space or more fails the test with the fourth pair.

title: A component with an undecided reference promise is not best of breed
when: With a component whose reference comparison is at its current contract set and lists one promise with no verdict: evaluate the specification.
then: It does not hold, and the undecided promise is named.
